subtopic: A power cut or rain spoils plans
subtype: Approach: finishing homework before the battery dies [Action]
passage: The storm warning crackled from the radio. "Ma, a storm is coming tonight," Sameer said, pulling the laptop closer. "So?" said his mother Sudha, stirring the dal. "So the online maths task is due tomorrow, and if the power goes, I lose it. I am doing it now." Forty minutes later he clicked Submit. "Done. Now I need the printer." "For what?" "The science notes. If there is no charge tomorrow, I still have paper." Sudha raised an eyebrow. "Since when do you plan like this?" Sameer grinned. "Since last time." At nine the lights went out. Warm under a blanket, Sameer read the printed pages by torchlight.

qa.q: What did Sameer print before the storm?
Why did Sameer decide to finish the online task early, and what was he worried about?
qa.a: He worried that a power cut would make him miss the deadline, so he wanted the task safely submitted.

qa.q: What other step could Sameer take against an outage, and why?
qa.a: He could charge the phone and laptop fully and keep a torch nearby, because he can keep working or reading if the lights go.

qa.q: How might Sudha feel seeing Sameer plan this well?
qa.a: Surprised and pleased, since she raised an eyebrow and asked since when he plans like this. 🙂

grounding: A boy finishes an online task early and prints notes before a storm, so a power cut cannot strand him.
